questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Laos?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Laos article.

questions.proof: Boats from Laos cannot get to the ocean using the Mekong because of rapids and waterfalls in the south of the country.[5] Laos is the least densely populated country in Southeast Asia, with 32 people per square kilometer.[6] A railway connection between Thailand and Laos has been operational since July 2024, with trains running to Khamsavath railway station in Vientiane prefecture.[7]

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Laos?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Laos on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Laos article.

questions.proof: It is bordered by Myanmar and by China to the northwest, by Vietnam to the east, by Cambodia to the south and by Thailand to the west.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The Mekong river forms a part of the western boundary with _____.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “boundary”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Laos article.

questions.proof: The Mekong river forms a part of the western boundary with Thailand.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “In 1949 it became independent from _____, as the Kingdom of Laos.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “independent”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Laos article, under the heading “History”.

questions.proof: In 1949 it became independent from France, as the Kingdom of Laos.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “2 months later, the authorities of North _____, established a support group for Pathet Lao, in Ban Nameo.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “North”. It names one thing, not an action.
